chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Marry the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt in place of the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister, without their permission.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his aunt while his cousin is still alive?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of marriage due to consanguinity (mahram) is absolute and independent of the consent of intermediate relatives, specifically noting that a man may marry his paternal or maternal aunt regardless of whether his cousins (the aunts' children) have given permission. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the bond of lineage creates an inherent barrier to marriage, distinct from the rights of other family members. It serves to resolve potential disputes in early Islamic society regarding the validity of marriages when intermediate heirs were alive.
